passage:
The following text is from Jane Austen's 1813 novel *Pride and Prejudice*. Mr. Bingley and his friend Mr. Darcy are attending a ball. Mrs. Bennet and her daughters are also guests.

Mr. Bingley had soon made himself acquainted with all the principal people in the room: he was lively and unreserved, danced every dance, was angry that the ball closed so early, and talked of giving one himself at Netherfield. Such amiable qualities must speak for themselves. What a contrast between him and his friend! Mr. Darcy danced only once with Mrs. Hurst and once with Miss Bingley, declined being introduced to any other lady, and spent the rest of the evening in walking about the room, speaking occasionally to one of his own party. … Amongst the most violent against him was Mrs. Bennet, whose dislike of his general behaviour was sharpened into particular resentment by his having slighted one of her daughters.
stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Mrs. Bennet's opinion of Mr. Darcy?
option_a: It is based partly on how he treated a member of her own family.
option_b: It is more favorable than the opinion held by most of the other guests.
option_c: It improved after Mr. Darcy danced with one of her daughters.
option_d: It was formed before she had ever seen Mr. Darcy.
explanation_en:
Mrs. Bennet disliked Mr. Darcy's “general behaviour,” but her dislike was “sharpened into particular resentment by his having slighted one of her daughters.” Her opinion therefore rests partly on how he treated her own daughter, as choice A says.

Choice B is wrong because she is “amongst the most violent against him,” so her opinion is not more favorable than others'. Choice C is wrong because Mr. Darcy “slighted” her daughter and danced only with Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley. Choice D is wrong because her resentment came from his behavior at the ball, which she observed.
explanation_uz:
Bennet xonimga janob Darsining “umumiy xulq-atvori” yoqmagan, ammo bu norozilik u “qizlaridan birini mensimagani” sababli “alohida adovatga aylangan.” Demak, uning fikri qisman Darsi uning qiziga qanday munosabatda bo‘lganiga asoslangan — to‘g‘ri javob A.

B noto‘g‘ri: u “Darsiga eng qattiq qarshi bo‘lganlar orasida,” demak uning fikri boshqalarnikidan ijobiyroq emas. C noto‘g‘ri: janob Darsi uning qizini “mensimagan” va faqat Xerst xonim hamda miss Bingli bilan raqsga tushgan. D noto‘g‘ri: uning adovati Darsining bal paytidagi xatti-harakatidan kelib chiqqan, buni esa u o‘z ko‘zi bilan ko‘rgan.

The following text is from Willa Cather's 1913 novel *O Pioneers!*

On the sidewalk in front of one of the stores sat a little Swede boy, crying bitterly. He was about five years old. … He cried quietly, and the few people who hurried by did not notice him. He was afraid to stop any one, afraid to go into the store and ask for help, so he sat wringing his long sleeves and looking up a telegraph pole beside him, whimpering, “My kitten, oh, my kitten! Her will fweeze!” … He was a little country boy, and this village was to him a very strange and perplexing place, where people wore fine clothes and had hard hearts. He always felt shy and awkward here, and wanted to hide behind things for fear some one might laugh at him.
stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about why the boy does not ask anyone for help?
option_a: He believes that his kitten will soon climb down on its own.
option_b: He feels out of place in the town and fears how the people there will treat him.
option_c: He has been told by his parents never to speak to strangers.
option_d: He thinks that no one in the town is strong enough to reach the kitten.
explanation_en:
The boy is “afraid to stop any one,” and the text explains that the village seems “strange and perplexing” to him, a place where people “had hard hearts,” and that he fears someone “might laugh at him.” It is reasonable to infer that he stays silent because he feels like an outsider and fears the townspeople's reaction, as choice B says.

Choice A is wrong because he is crying and worried that the kitten “will fweeze” (freeze), which shows he does not expect it to come down safely. Choice C is wrong because the text never mentions any instructions from his parents. Choice D is wrong because nothing suggests he doubts anyone's strength; his fear concerns how people will treat him.
explanation_uz:
Bola “hech kimni to‘xtatishga qo‘rqadi”; matnda shaharcha unga “g‘alati va tushunarsiz,” odamlari “tosh yurak” joy bo‘lib tuyulgani va kimdir “ustidan kulishidan” qo‘rqishi aytiladi. Demak, u o‘zini begona his qilgani va shahar aholisining munosabatidan qo‘rqqani uchun indamay o‘tiradi, degan xulosa mantiqiy — to‘g‘ri javob B.

A noto‘g‘ri: u yig‘layapti va mushukcha “muzlab qoladi” deb xavotirda, ya’ni u mushukcha o‘zi eson-omon tushadi deb o‘ylamaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: matnda ota-onasining biror ko‘rsatmasi tilga olinmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: u birovning kuchiga shubha qilayotgani haqida ishora yo‘q; uning qo‘rquvi odamlar unga qanday munosabatda bo‘lishi bilan bog‘liq.

passage: Over one summer, ecologist Bakhrom Tursunov counted the bees visiting two neighboring sunflower fields. The fields were planted on the same day with the same seed, but one was bordered by a strip of wildflowers and the other was not. Tursunov counted nearly twice as many bees in the field with the wildflower strip, and that field also produced noticeably more sunflower seeds. Because sunflowers produce more seeds when more of their flowers are pollinated, these results suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: sunflowers produce more seeds when they are planted later in the season.
option_b: bees generally avoid fields that are bordered by wildflowers.
option_c: the wildflower strip may have drawn more bees to the area, leading to more pollination of the sunflowers.
option_d: the field without the wildflower strip received more rain during the summer.
explanation_en:
The field with the wildflower strip had nearly twice as many bees and more seeds, and the text notes that more pollination leads to more seeds. The most logical conclusion is that the wildflowers attracted bees that then pollinated the sunflowers, as choice C says.

Choice A is wrong because both fields were planted on the same day. Choice B contradicts the results: the field bordered by wildflowers had more bees. Choice D is unsupported: the text gives no information about rainfall.
explanation_uz:
Yovvoyi gullar chizig‘i bo‘lgan dalada asalarilar deyarli ikki baravar ko‘p va urug‘ ham ko‘proq bo‘lgan; matnda ko‘proq changlanish ko‘proq urug‘ berishi ham aytilgan. Eng mantiqiy xulosa — yovvoyi gullar asalarilarni jalb qilgan, ular esa kungaboqarlarni changlatgan. To‘g‘ri javob — C.

A noto‘g‘ri: ikkala dala ham bir kunda ekilgan. B natijalarga zid: yovvoyi gullar bilan o‘ralgan dalada asalarilar ko‘proq bo‘lgan. D asossiz: matnda yog‘ingarchilik haqida ma’lumot yo‘q.

passage:
The following text is from Zitkala-Ša's 1900 memoir “Impressions of an Indian Childhood.” The narrator, a young Dakota girl, is walking home from the river with her mother, who carries water for the family.

So I said: “Mother, when I am tall as my cousin Warca-Ziwin, you shall not have to come for water. I will do it for you.” With a strange tremor in her voice which I could not understand, she answered, “If the paleface does not take away from us the river we drink.” … Setting the pail of water on the ground, my mother stooped, and stretching her left hand out on the level with my eyes, she placed her other arm about me; she pointed to the hill where my uncle and my only sister lay buried. “There is what the paleface has done! Since then your father too has been buried in a hill nearer the rising sun. We were once very happy. But the paleface has stolen our lands and driven us hither.”
stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the mother's response to her daughter's promise?
option_a: The mother is annoyed that her daughter admires her cousin so much.
option_b: The mother doubts that her daughter will ever grow as tall as her cousin.
option_c: The mother expects the family to return soon to the land where they once lived happily.
option_d: The mother fears that the family may lose even the river they now depend on, just as they lost their land before.
explanation_en:
The daughter promises to carry water when she is older, and the mother answers with “a strange tremor,” adding, “If the paleface does not take away from us the river we drink.” She then explains that the family's land was “stolen” and they were “driven” to this place. Her reply suggests she fears losing the river too, as choice D says.

Choice A is wrong because the mother never reacts to the cousin; her concern is the river. Choice B is wrong because her condition (“If the paleface does not take away…”) concerns the river, not her daughter's height. Choice C is wrong because she says the family was “driven” away and expresses no expectation of returning.
explanation_uz:
Qizcha katta bo‘lganida suvni o‘zi tashishini va’da qiladi, onasi esa “g‘alati titroq ovoz” bilan javob beradi: “Agar oq yuzli bizdan ichadigan daryomizni tortib olmasa.” So‘ng u oilaning yerlari “o‘g‘irlangani” va ular bu yerga “haydab kelingani”ni tushuntiradi. Uning javobi daryodan ham ayrilib qolishdan qo‘rqayotganini ko‘rsatadi — to‘g‘ri javob D.

A noto‘g‘ri: ona jiyani haqida hech qanday munosabat bildirmaydi, uning tashvishi — daryo. B noto‘g‘ri: uning sharti (“Agar oq yuzli tortib olmasa…”) qizining bo‘yi haqida emas, daryo haqida. C noto‘g‘ri: u oila “haydab chiqarilgan”ini aytadi va qaytib borishni kutayotganini bildirmaydi.

The following text is from the Introduction to the 1872 edition of Charles Darwin's *On the Origin of Species*. Darwin is outlining the chapters of the book.

This fundamental subject of natural selection will be treated at some length in the fourth chapter; and we shall then see how natural selection almost inevitably causes much extinction of the less improved forms of life, and leads to what I have called divergence of character. In the next chapter I shall discuss the complex and little known laws of variation. In the five succeeding chapters, the most apparent and gravest difficulties in accepting the theory will be given: namely, first, the difficulties of transitions … secondly the subject of instinct, or the mental powers of animals; thirdly, hybridism … and fourthly, the imperfection of the geological record.
stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about Darwin's approach in the book?
option_a: He believes that his theory faces no serious difficulties.
option_b: He considers the laws of variation to be fully understood.
option_c: He intends to devote a large part of the book to addressing objections that readers might raise against his theory.
option_d: He plans to discuss the geological record before he discusses natural selection.
explanation_en:
Darwin says that “five succeeding chapters” will present “the most apparent and gravest difficulties in accepting the theory.” Giving several whole chapters to these difficulties suggests that he plans to take objections seriously and address them at length, as choice C says.

Choice A is wrong because he calls some difficulties “gravest,” acknowledging that they are serious. Choice B is wrong because he calls the laws of variation “complex and little known.” Choice D is wrong because natural selection comes in the fourth chapter, while the geological record is part of the difficulties discussed in later chapters.
explanation_uz:
Darvin “keyingi beshta bob”da “nazariyani qabul qilishdagi eng ko‘zga tashlanadigan va eng jiddiy qiyinchiliklar” keltirilishini aytadi. Bu qiyinchiliklarga bir nechta to‘liq bob ajratilishi uning e’tirozlarga jiddiy qarashini va ularni batafsil ko‘rib chiqmoqchi ekanini ko‘rsatadi — to‘g‘ri javob C.

A noto‘g‘ri: u ba’zi qiyinchiliklarni “eng jiddiy” deb ataydi, ya’ni ularning jiddiyligini tan oladi. B noto‘g‘ri: u o‘zgaruvchanlik qonunlarini “murakkab va kam o‘rganilgan” deb ataydi. D noto‘g‘ri: tabiiy tanlanish to‘rtinchi bobda keladi, geologik yilnoma esa keyingi boblarda muhokama qilinadigan qiyinchiliklar qatorida.

passage: Astronomers monitoring a distant star noticed that its brightness dips by the same small amount every 41 days, with each dip lasting about six hours. When they examined older telescope images of the star taken over the previous decade, they found dips of the same size occurring on the same 41-day schedule throughout. Because a small, brief dip in a star's brightness can occur when a planet passes between the star and observers on Earth, the regularity of these dips suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: the star's brightness has steadily declined over the past decade.
option_b: the dips began only recently and are likely to stop soon.
option_c: the telescopes used in the older images were not working properly.
option_d: the dips may be caused by a planet that orbits the star once every 41 days.
explanation_en:
The dips repeat every 41 days with the same size and duration, and they have done so for a decade. Since a planet passing in front of a star can cause such a dip, a dip that recurs on a fixed schedule suggests an object, such as a planet, orbiting the star every 41 days. Choice D follows logically.

Choice A is wrong because the text describes repeated brief dips, not a steady decline. Choice B contradicts the older images, which show the dips occurring throughout the past decade. Choice C is unsupported: the older images match the newer observations, which gives no reason to think the telescopes were faulty.
explanation_uz:
Yorqinlikning pasayishlari har 41 kunda bir xil kattalik va davomiylikda takrorlanadi va bu o‘n yildan beri davom etmoqda. Sayyora yulduz oldidan o‘tganda shunday pasayish yuz berishi mumkinligi sababli, qat’iy jadval bo‘yicha takrorlanadigan pasayish yulduz atrofida har 41 kunda aylanadigan jism, masalan, sayyora borligini ko‘rsatadi. D javob mantiqan kelib chiqadi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda doimiy pasayish emas, takroriy qisqa pasayishlar tasvirlangan. B eski tasvirlarga zid: ular pasayishlar so‘nggi o‘n yil davomida bo‘lganini ko‘rsatadi. C asossiz: eski tasvirlar yangi kuzatuvlarga mos keladi, demak teleskoplar nosoz bo‘lgan deyishga asos yo‘q.

passage:
The following text is from Mark Twain's 1883 memoir *Life on the Mississippi*. As a boy, Twain longed to work on a steamboat. Here he describes another boy from his town who had found such a job.

That boy had been notoriously worldly, and I just the reverse; yet he was exalted to this eminence, and I left in obscurity and misery. There was nothing generous about this fellow in his greatness. He would always manage to have a rusty bolt to scrub while his boat tarried at our town, and he would sit on the inside guard and scrub it, where we could all see him and envy him and loathe him. … When his boat blew up at last, it diffused a tranquil contentment among us such as we had not known for months. But when he came home the next week, alive, renowned, and appeared in church all battered up and bandaged, a shining hero, stared at and wondered over by everybody, it seemed to us that the partiality of Providence for an undeserving reptile had reached a point where it was open to criticism.
stem: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be inferred about the narrator's attitude toward the boy?
option_a: The narrator believed the boy deserved his success because he worked harder than the other boys.
option_b: The narrator's dislike of the boy was driven largely by envy of the attention and admiration the boy received.
option_c: The narrator admired the boy for being modest about his job on the steamboat.
option_d: The narrator was relieved and grateful when the boy returned home safely after the accident.
explanation_en:
The narrator admits that the boys would “envy him and loathe him,” and he complains that this “undeserving” boy got the job while he himself was left “in obscurity and misery.” Even the boy's survival is resented because he came home “a shining hero, stared at and wondered over by everybody.” The humorous exaggeration shows that the narrator's dislike grew mainly from envy of the boy's glory, as choice B says.

Choice A is wrong because the narrator calls the boy “undeserving” and says nothing about hard work; the rusty bolt is scrubbed for show, “where we could all see him.” Choice C is wrong because the boy shows off, so he is not modest. Choice D is wrong because the boys felt “tranquil contentment” when the boat blew up and treated his return as unfair luck, not as a relief.
explanation_uz:
Hikoyachi bolalar unga “havas qilib, undan nafratlanganini” tan oladi va bu “noloyiq” bola ishga joylashgani, o‘zi esa “nomsiz va baxtsiz” qolganidan nolinadi. Hatto bolaning omon qolgani ham alam qiladi, chunki u “hamma tikilib, hayratlanib qaraydigan porloq qahramon” bo‘lib qaytgan. Bu kulgili mubolag‘a hikoyachining nafrati asosan bolaning shon-shuhratiga bo‘lgan hasaddan kelib chiqqanini ko‘rsatadi — to‘g‘ri javob B.

A noto‘g‘ri: hikoyachi bolani “noloyiq” deb ataydi va mehnatsevarligi haqida hech narsa demaydi; zanglagan boltni u ko‘z-ko‘z qilish uchun, “hammamiz ko‘radigan joyda” tozalaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: bola maqtanadi, demak u kamtar emas. D noto‘g‘ri: kema portlaganda bolalar “osuda mamnuniyat” his qilgan va uning qaytishini adolatsiz omad deb bilgan, yengil tortish deb emas.

passage: Scholars have long assumed that a collection of undated letters by the merchant Hasan Bekov was written during the 1840s, when records show he was living in the city of Marvan. Historian Gulnora Ismoilova points out, however, that several of the letters mention goods arriving “by the new railway,” and that the railway to Marvan was not completed until 1879. Records also show that Bekov was still alive and trading in 1885. Taken together, these facts suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
option_a: at least some of the letters were probably written after 1879, decades later than scholars have assumed.
option_b: none of the letters in the collection could have been written in the 1840s.
option_c: Bekov had moved away from Marvan before the railway was completed.
option_d: the records showing when the railway to Marvan was completed are inaccurate.
explanation_en:
Several letters mention “the new railway,” which reached Marvan only in 1879, and Bekov was still alive and trading in 1885. Those letters were therefore most likely written after 1879, which conflicts with the assumption that the collection dates from the 1840s. Choice A states this conclusion with appropriate caution.

Choice B goes too far: only “several” letters mention the railway, so the others could still date from the 1840s. Choice C is unsupported; nothing in the text indicates where Bekov lived after the 1840s, and letters mentioning the railway's arrival suggest a connection to Marvan, not a move away. Choice D is unsupported: Ismoilova relies on the railway date, and nothing suggests it is wrong.
explanation_uz:
Bir nechta maktubda “yangi temir yo‘l” tilga olinadi, temir yo‘l esa Marvanga faqat 1879-yilda yetib kelgan; Bekov 1885-yilda ham tirik bo‘lib, savdo bilan shug‘ullangan. Demak, o‘sha maktublar katta ehtimol bilan 1879-yildan keyin yozilgan, bu esa to‘plam 1840-yillarga tegishli degan taxminga zid. A javob bu xulosani kerakli ehtiyotkorlik bilan ifodalaydi.

B haddan oshib ketadi: temir yo‘lni faqat “bir nechta” maktub tilga oladi, qolganlari hali ham 1840-yillarda yozilgan bo‘lishi mumkin. C asossiz: matnda Bekov 1840-yillardan keyin qayerda yashagani aytilmagan, temir yo‘l orqali yuk kelganini eslatuvchi maktublar esa Marvandan ketganini emas, u bilan aloqani ko‘rsatadi. D asossiz: Ismoilova temir yo‘l sanasiga tayanadi va uning noto‘g‘ri ekaniga hech qanday ishora yo‘q.
